To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
theory of mind activates a core-network of brain regions, and that this core-network is modulated by a number of task and stimulus factors.
the core-network of theory of mind is composed of the mPFC (BA 9 and 10), the bilateral posterior TPJs (BA 39 and 40), the bilateral precunei (BA 7) and the left superior parietal lobule (BA 7).
the mPFC (BA 10) and the bilateral posterior TPJs (BA 39/40) constitute a core-network for theory of mind.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the brain processes social information and how it is related to our understanding of other people's mental states.
the functional organization and functional specialization of the neural correlates of the theory of mind.
the question of whether there is a common neural basis for reasoning about mental states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain regions involved in theory of mind are not fixed, but depend on the task and the stimulus-format used.
theory of mind is a complex and multifaceted cognitive process that engages multiple brain regions and networks, which are not necessarily specific to theory of mind.
theory of mind is not a unitary phenomenon but a complex cognitive ability, with multiple sub-components that rely on a core network of brain areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

theory of mind involves the activation of a core-network of brain regions that are involved in the representation of mental states and the integration of these representations into a coherent mental model.
the core-network of theory of mind is composed of the mPFC (especially ventral mPFC and dorsal anterior cingulate) and the bilateral posterior TPJs.
the TPJ and the mPFC form the core network for theory-of-mind, and that the precuneus and the inferior frontal gyrus are involved in the processing of complex stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural network for theory of minds is highly complex.
the neural basis of theory of mind is not unitary.

the functional architecture of theory of mind is more complex than the core-network idea suggests, but that the core-network idea remains a useful starting point for further research on theory of mind.
